content_of_post_to_answer: Why do we feel stressed even when there is no serious problem in our lives?
answer: Stress is not always a response to a problem; often it is a response to uncertainty, unfinished thoughts, or a mind constantly scanning for what could go wrong. The brain evolved to notice threats, not to measure whether life is objectively safe. I've written more about this pattern on my profile for anyone interested in going deeper. A quiet life can still feel stressful when the mind never gets a signal that it is allowed to rest.
